## What DiffPTM does

A modified peptide's intensity changes when the modification changes **and** when its
protein changes. DiffPTM separates the two questions:

* **differential PTM abundance (DPA)**: does the site change between conditions, whatever
  the reason?
* **differential PTM usage (DPU)**: does the site change *relative to its protein*? This
  needs the total-proteome table and is the test DiffPTM is built for.

Three statistical methods answer the usage question and can be run side by side on the same
processed data: the single model (limma; paired when the PTM and proteome samples share
their names), MSstatsPTM (model then correct) and msqrob2PTM (correct then model). They
give the same usage fold changes but different standard errors. By default the single model
pairs each site with its protein sample by sample (per-site paired single model, the limma
analysis of the within-sample differences); the consensus version, which shares one
correlation between all sites, gains degrees of freedom but assumes that a site and its
protein vary alike, which `dpu_diagnostics()` checks. MSstatsPTM is the choice when the two
fractions do not come from the same samples.

Every usage test assumes that, without a usage change, a site follows its protein one to one.
`usage_beta_check()` refits the usage model with the protein term scaled by 0.8 and 1.2 and
flags the calls that do not survive; calls on sites whose protein changes strongly are the
least robust and are worth confirming by another method. Normalisation sets the reference of
usage: the default global centring removes a between-condition shift of the enriched fraction,
which is right when loading is not controlled but removes a genuine global change of
modification (for example after stimulation); per-condition centring is available for
experiments in which loading is controlled independently.

## Starting the interface

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(DiffPTM)
run_app()
```

The interface opens in the browser and runs on your computer: no data leave it. It is
organised in six steps, each a page of the left menu. Every step calls exported functions of
the package, so an analysis done in the interface can be reproduced in R from the saved
session (see the last section).

## 1. Import

Choose the software, upload the **total-proteome table** and the **PTM table** and click
*Import*. The formats accepted for each software are listed in the Help page and in the
vignettes *DiffPTM with MaxQuant*, *... with Spectronaut*, *... with Proteome Discoverer*,
*... with FragPipe* and *... with DIA-NN*.

Intensities are expected raw (the app applies log2). Untick *Intensities are raw* for tables
already on the log2 scale (FragPipe TMT-Integrator); the app warns when the scale looks wrong.

*Load example dataset* loads a simulated label-free experiment (1,500 proteins, 800
phosphosites, two conditions with four samples each) with its design, to try the interface.

## 2. Design

Every sample needs a **condition**. Two ways to fill the tables: *Pre-fill from sample
names*, which cuts the names at the separator and uses the chosen tokens (`-1` means
everything but the last token, i.e. the name without its replicate number), or upload an
annotation table (`sample`, `condition`, optional `factor`, `subject`, `mixture`). Cells
can be edited by double-clicking. Samples left without a condition are excluded.

**Sample names must match between the two tables for the paired analysis.** When the
PTM and proteome runs of the same biological sample have different names, which is the rule
(`Phospho_mock_1` and `mock_1` in a combined MaxQuant search; `Phospho-01_NS_R1` and
`Proteome-01_NS_R1` in Spectronaut), give each table a regular expression whose capture
group is the common name. Samples that do not match the expression are dropped, which also
removes the proteome runs that a MaxQuant site table lists alongside the enriched runs. The
preview under the fields tells how many samples are kept and how many names are shared.

Optional columns: a **second factor** (time point, batch; contrasts are built within each
level and ComBat can use it), a **subject** for paired designs across conditions (used as a
blocking factor) and the **TMT mixture**.

## 3. Processing

* *Filtering*: reverse hits and contaminants; site rows repeated for several protein
  accessions with identical quantities (Spectronaut); minimal localization probability;
  minimal number (and percentage) of observed values in at least one group.
* *PTM to protein matching*: by identifier (fast) or by locating the peptide sequence in the
  FASTA of the search (robust to differences of protein inference between the two
  searches). For peptide tables without site positions (DIA-NN precursors, FragPipe
  modified peptides) the FASTA also gives the site positions.
* *Normalisation*: per-condition median centering (default), global median, ComBat, none.
* *Imputation*: off by default. The three methods fit on observed values; imputing before
  the correction inflates false discoveries.

The **quality-control** plots show, for each table: the number of features observed per
sample (runs that quantified far fewer features than the others stand out and should be
removed in step 2), the Jaccard index of detection between samples with the conditions as a
colour strip, a PCA and the intensity distributions. The processing log lists every
operation; it becomes the Materials & Methods paragraph of the report.

## 4. Statistics

Choose the methods (the single model is always available; MSstatsPTM and msqrob2PTM when
installed), the analyses (protein abundance, PTM abundance, PTM usage), the contrasts (each
condition against a reference, every pair, or each condition against the others), the
π₀-aware FDR procedure, the FDR threshold and an optional fold-change threshold (1 = none,
the recommended setting for usage).

## 5. Results

For the selected analysis, contrast and method: a volcano plot labelled with gene and site,
the raw p-value histogram (flat with a peak near 0 when the test is well calibrated), the
PTM-vs-protein fold-change plot (points off the diagonal change in usage), the number of
significant features per contrast and method, the agreement between methods, the table of
significant features and the detection-discordance table (PTM features observed in samples
where their protein was not quantified, which no quantitative test can use).

## 6. Download

An Excel workbook with every table, a README sheet and the Materials & Methods paragraph;
the figures as an editable PowerPoint and as PDF; and the session as an `.rds` file.

## Reproducing an interface analysis in R

The `.rds` session contains the processed experiment (`x`), the results (`res`), the
contrasts and the thresholds:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
s <- readRDS("DiffPTM_session.rds")
s$x                              # processed ptm_experiment, with its log
head(s$res)                      # tidy results: feature_id, analysis, contrast, log2FC, se, statistic, pvalue, adj_pvalue, method
cat(methods_paragraph(s$x, s$methods))
plot_volcano(subset(s$res, analysis == "ptm_DPU" & contrast == s$contrasts$name[1] & method == "limma"), s$fdr)
```

The same analysis from scratch, with the example dataset shipped in the package:

```{r example}
library(DiffPTM)
ex <- system.file("extdata", "example", package = "DiffPTM")
prot <- import_protein(file.path(ex, "protein.tsv"), "Generic")
ptm  <- import_ptm(file.path(ex, "ptm.tsv"), "Generic")
ann  <- read_annotation(file.path(ex, "annotation.tsv"))
x <- new_ptm_experiment(prot, ptm, annotation = list(protein = ann, ptm = ann)) |>
  filter_localization(0.75) |> filter_min_observed(min_n = 2) |>
  normalise(method = "global_median") |> match_ptm_to_protein("id")
x
res <- run_methods(x, make_contrasts(x), methods = "limma", pi0_method = "bh")
table(res$analysis, res$adj_pvalue < 0.05)
```

```{r example-plots, fig.height = 5}
r <- subset(res, analysis == "ptm_DPU")
r$label <- x$ptm$meta$label[match(r$feature_id, x$ptm$meta$feature_id)]
plot_volcano(r, fdr = 0.05, title = "PTM usage, treated vs control")
```
